_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never shipped to the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated. English-only. Keep activityId/version in sync with config.json.

markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of their own Investigation Record entries (for example a lens/total magnification with its sharpness percentage, or the Onion Slide observations at ×4, ×10 and ×40) as evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine entries from the student's own record, e.g. '×4 total ×40 sharp 100%' and '×40 total ×400 nucleus clear'; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim such as 'it got bigger' with no logged entry quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Describes how the picture changed as magnification increased from ×4 to ×40: fewer cells are visible, each looks larger (the field of view gets smaller), and/or the range of sharp focus becomes tiny.
markingScheme.accept: 'You see less of the slide but bigger cells'; 'the view gets smaller/zoomed in'; 'harder to focus at ×40'.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why to start at the lowest power and use the FINE knob at high power: low power has a wide field so the sample is easy to find, and a high-power lens sits very close to the slide so the coarse knob could crack the slide, so only small fine-focus adjustments are safe.
markingScheme.accept: Either reason for starting low (easy to find the sample / avoid hitting the slide) together with fine focus only at high power.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'Because it's the rule' or 'to be safe' with no reason given.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies Slide 1 as the plant cell and gives the cell wall (thick, regular outline / fixed box shape) as the reason.
markingScheme.accept: 'Slide 1 because plant cells have a cell wall giving a regular shape'; mention of the nucleus alone is not enough (both cell types have one).
markingScheme.insufficient: Choosing Slide 1 with no feature given, or citing the nucleus as the difference.

markingScheme.criterion: Contrasts it with Slide 2: no cell wall, so irregular rounded shape, typical of an animal cell.
markingScheme.accept: 'Slide 2 is probably animal because animal cells have no cell wall so they are not fixed in shape'.

markingScheme.criterion: Describes the safe order for reaching ×400: start with the lowest-power (×4) objective, use the coarse knob to find the cells, fine focus, then switch to ×10 then ×40 (with a ×10 eyepiece) refocusing with the FINE knob only; stage lowered first and slide secured.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct low-to-high sequence that ends at ×40 objective with fine focus only; ×10 eyepiece × ×40 objective = ×400 stated or implied.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'put on the ×40 lens' immediately, or using coarse focus at ×40.

levels.descriptor: No logged entries quoted, no description of how the view changed, and no correct reason for starting at low power.
One of the three analytic points met: quotes two real entries, OR describes the change from ×4 to ×40, OR explains low power first / fine focus only at high power.
Two of the three analytic points met, e.g. quotes real entries and describes the change but gives no reason for the procedure.

All three analytic points present: quotes at least two of their own entries, describes fewer/larger cells and smaller field from ×4 to ×40, and explains why to start low and use only fine focus at high power.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: Does not identify the plant slide using the cell wall and gives no safe procedure.
One of the three analytic points met: Slide 1 as plant with the cell wall reason, OR the contrast with Slide 2, OR a correct safe order to ×400.
Two of the three analytic points met, e.g. correct plant slide with cell-wall reasoning and contrast, but no safe procedure.

All three analytic points present: Slide 1 identified as plant because of the cell wall, Slide 2 contrasted as animal (no wall, irregular), and a correct low-to-high procedure ending with the fine knob at ×40 (×400 total).

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed; no correct scientific vocabulary.

Main meaning understandable, but organisation or precision is weak, or key terms (objective, eyepiece, magnification, fine focus, cell wall, nucleus) are missing or misused. Do not deduct for minor spelling/grammar slips that do not harm meaning.
Clear, logically organised full sentences using correct scientific vocabulary, precise enough to follow easily. Minor spelling/grammar slips that do not affect meaning are not penalised.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply), using each question's point-by-point marking_scheme (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands - do not invent extra criteria. The Explain marks ARE the use_of_evidence criterion and the Apply marks ARE the reasoning criterion (one-to-one); never award them twice. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Communication is judged holistically across both answers and never overlaps the content marks. Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept'; do not penalise spelling or grammar unless it makes the meaning unclear. Use the raw Investigation Record data (not just the student's summary) to verify any claim about their own entries (lens, total magnification, sharpness). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
